summary: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' Ministry of National Security grants entry permits on arrival of up to six months to visitors from the UK, the US, the Schengen countries and CARICOM and up to three months to others, extendable at the Immigration Head Office, and an indefinite stay to OECS nationals. The nationalities the Ministry names — Afghanistan, Cameroon, China, the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Nigeria and Syria — must apply to it for an entry visa in advance; for other nationalities no official page we could read says whether a visa is needed.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says most visits are trouble-free, but there have been crimes including murder, armed robbery and assault, and an increase in gang-related murders involving guns, some in populated and public areas. It advises avoiding isolated areas, including beaches, after dark and taking particular care around street and beach parties. Canada's travel advice says the hurricane season is from early June to the end of November and that the La Soufrière volcano is active, its last significant eruption having been in April 2021.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says the hurricane season is from early June to the end of November, and that during this period even small tropical storms can quickly develop into major hurricanes.

Canada's travel advice says the La Soufrière volcano on St. Vincent is active and that its last significant eruption was in April 2021. It says there is limited police presence in the northern part of Saint Vincent island, namely Falls of Baleine, La Soufrière and Trinity Falls, and advises caution if trekking there.

Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' Ministry of National Security says visitors who wish to stay longer than the period given on arrival can apply for an extension at the Immigration Head Office in Kingstown or at the Bequia, Mustique, Canouan or Union Island ports, at EC$75 cash per month or part of a month. The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to stay longer than the period allowed.

Canada's travel advice says U.S. dollars are also widely accepted. The UK government says taxis are not metered, that there are set fares for most destinations, to agree the fare in local currency with the driver before you set off, and that you can often pay in US dollars.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Saint Vincent and the Grenadines?
faq.answer: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' Ministry of National Security says persons from Afghanistan, Cameroon, China, the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Nigeria and Syria must apply to it for an entry visa, with a non-refundable fee of EC$200. The UK and US governments' travel advice tells their citizens they need no visa, and Canada's says none is required for stays up to 30 days; Türkiye's Foreign Ministry says Turkish ordinary passport holders need one. An agreement between the EU and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines lets citizens of EU Member States other than Ireland stay without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. For other nationalities no official page we could read says whether a visa is needed. The Ministry says entry permits granted on arrival run up to six months for visitors from CARICOM, the UK, the Schengen countries and the US and up to three months for others; OECS nationals get an indefinite stay.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines?
faq.answer: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' Ministry of National Security says entry permits are granted on arrival by an immigration officer: up to six months for CARICOM, UK, Schengen and US nationals, and up to three months for other countries. To stay longer, you can apply for an extension at the Immigration Head Office in Kingstown or at the Bequia, Mustique, Canouan or Union Island ports; it costs EC$75 cash per month or part of a month.

faq.question: What applies to CARICOM citizens?
faq.answer: The Ministry of National Security says CARICOM nationals are granted an entry permit of up to six months on arrival and OECS nationals an indefinite stay, and that CARICOM citizens holding a CSME certificate issued in their own country may work for six months pending an upgraded certificate from the Ministry.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate?
faq.answer: Only if you are coming from a country listed as a yellow fever transmission risk, according to the UK Foreign Office; WHO's country list says proof of vaccination is required for travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission.
